title: Historical Posters
summary: A nine-week poster series translating historical design movements into contemporary compositions through research, thumbnail studies, and visual experimentation.

hero.alt: Looping preview of the historical posters.

overview.challenge: A collection of poster designs inspired by historical design movements and visual traditions.
overview.solution: Each poster translates a researched design movement into a contemporary composition, moving between strict grids, dynamic geometry, collage, and minimal symbolism.
overview.outcome: The nine-week series resulted in nine finished posters and written reflections, with Dada, the Stenberg Brothers, and Modernism among the strongest directions.
overview._notes: Copy refined to reflect the documented project process.

blocks.label: 01 — Research
blocks.alt: Research references for the poster series.
blocks.heading: Nine movements, nine visual systems
blocks.body: Each movement began with research into its context, visual conventions, and influential designers. Comparing these references helped identify which formal ideas—such as collage, geometry, grids, or reduction—could be reinterpreted rather than copied.

blocks.label: 02 — Sketches
blocks.heading: From thumbnail to final poster
blocks.body: I developed thumbnail compositions before moving into digital drafts, testing hierarchy, contrast, and movement. The final series preserves the character of each movement while making every poster work as a distinct contemporary piece.

blocks.label: 03 — Concept development
blocks.alt: Concept development for the poster series.
blocks.heading: Translating history into contemporary work
blocks.body: Rather than applying one style across the entire series, I adapted the visual logic of each movement to the subject. The changing compositions show how research can guide design decisions while still leaving room for interpretation.
